Participant age and sex (young male smokers and matched nonsmokers), cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3T Philips), and processing software (SPM8, FSL) are all reported (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (study includes whole-brain task activation maps and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This empirical study used fMRI (with concurrent EEG group) to assess nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs neutral pictures) within participants, and reports whole-brain task-evoked analyses (2×2 ANOVA, FWE-corrected activations with coordinates). Participant demographics (age comparison and sex distribution) and cue type are reported; scanner acquisition and preprocessing details are referenced in the fMRI data acquisition/preprocessing subsection and Supporting Information (supplementary materials included). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking cue videos (nicotine) with within-participant contrasts (smoking videos > control videos). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed (FLAME, TFCE-corrected) and whole-brain activation results are reported in the text/figures/tables. Relevant participant information (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL) are provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) are met.

This publication is a narrative review of functional neuroimaging (fMRI and MRS) studies in drug abusers and does not report original empirical fMRI data. Exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original human fMRI data) applies. No original within-participant drug-cue > control contrast is reported as a primary analysis (I3 and I4 not met). The paper does not provide a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from an original experiment (I5 not met). Required primary-study details for inclusion (participant age/sex per primary dataset, cue type tied to an original analysis, scanner field strength, processing software) are not provided as results of an original fMRI experiment (I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I5, I7. Full text appears complete (contains intro, methods of review, results, discussion, references), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with individualwithin-subject contrasts of food>neutral and group-level voxelwise analyses. The manuscript includes whole-brain exploratory analyses (1-sample t test, FWE-corrected, reported clusters; Figures and Tables report task-evoked maps), as well as ROI analyses; participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward-related cues (images of a $100 bill vs a blurry rectangle) and reports within-subject contrasts of reward>nonreward. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and thresholded (z>3.1, cluster p<.05) with results reported in tables/figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (money reward), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study that includes visual alcohol cue stimuli (90 pictures of alcoholic and neutral beverages), reports within-subject contrasts (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages), and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI 3dMVM, cluster-based FWE correction reported). Participant age and sex (females 21–65), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T, multiple vendors), and processing software (AFNI) are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task activation maps). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts (all food > non-food; high-calorie > low-calorie), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and cluster coordinates, and provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports voxelwise analyses restricted to an a priori ROI mask (not an unmasked, whole-brain group-level activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-subject smoking-cue > control-cue contrast was created), I6 (peak coordinates and cluster locations are reported), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [SPM8] are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain, unmasked voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported; analyses were restricted to an ROI mask). Full text appears complete.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual/object cues (I3). The analysis includes within-participant contrasts comparing cigarette versus control cue (cigarette>control) and reports a main effect of cue (I4). Group-level whole-brain, voxelwise activation maps were computed and thresholded (cluster-corrected), with results reported as coordinates and figures (I5, I6). Required methodological details are provided: participant age and sex (male, 18–45), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3-Tesla), and processing software (AFNI, FSL, etc.) (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical limitations). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual Pavlovian cues and food images. The study includes within-subject contrasts of food-outcome cues vs. a no-outcome control cue and reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses (permutation-based voxelwise testing; exploratory whole-brain results referenced). Participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a clinical pilot study assessing heroin craving via self-report (VAS) in methadone-maintained patients; it does not involve functional MRI, nor a visual cue-reactivity paradigm. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI study using visual stimuli), and consequently also fails I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5/I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or coordinate/figure-reported whole-brain results), and I7 (no MRI scanner field strength or processing software reported). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are specifically triggered. Exclude for not meeting required fMRI/cue-reactivity inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (no-go unhealthy food vs go healthy food; analyses collapsing food cues) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (3dMVM) with tables/figures of significant clusters. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (AFNI, ANTs, AFNI 3dMVM, SPSS) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject task activation maps). Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food images (natural reward cues) and meets all inclusion criteria. It uses within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood (food vs nonfood) across sessions, reports group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates and t-values for activated clusters, and also reports whole-brain regression results (FWE-corrected) for parametric modulation. Participant age and sex (young adult males), cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study used fMRI and presented tobacco images during a Smoking Pleasantness task (I3) and reports group-level whole-brain maps (for the interoceptive attention task) with coordinates (I5, I6) and participant demographics and cue type (I7). However, there is no reported within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or a whole-brain, task-evoked cue-reactivity analysis: imaging analyses focus on an interoceptive attention task and resting-state connectivity, not a voxelwise cue-reactivity contrast. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4 and cannot be included in the cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is an fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3: methamphetamine cue pictures); it includes a within-participant contrast of Methamphetamine Cue > Control Cue (I4); it reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps with cluster-corrected Z-statistic images (I5) and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables (I6); and it reports participant age/sex, cue type (methamphetamine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task whole-brain activation maps, and is empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with within-participant smoking>neutral contrasts and adequate reporting of participant demographics and scanner/processing details. However, the neuroimaging results are reported primarily as ROI-based analyses (PCC) and the only voxel-wise group analysis was restricted to the PCC (small-volume/ROI-restricted analysis). There is no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map or whole-brain coordinates/figures described that would satisfy a whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map requirement. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) with within-subject contrasts (hedonic food images > nonfood objects). Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise random-effects maps (voxel-wise p<0.01, cluster-level FDR q<0.05) reported in figures and tables of coordinates. Relevant participant information (age range, sex distribution), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes unmasked task effects). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study is not an fMRI task activation study. It reports EEG/ERP (LORETA) cue-reactivity and DTI/fiber-tracking results following tDCS in alcohol and crack-cocaine users, but does not provide any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise fMRI task-evoked statistical maps for drug- or natural reward-related visual cue contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (relevant participant and imaging acquisition details reported: male participants, cue types, MRI scanner field strength for DTI, processing software for EEG/DTI). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a functional MRI study assessing cue-reactivity), I4 (no documented within-participant fMRI contrast of drug cues>control stimuli), I5 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI activation maps). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) specifically apply, but failure to meet the required fMRI-related inclusion criteria mandates exclusion.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation using visual drug-cue stimuli (drug-related pictures) with within-subject contrasts of drug cues > neutral cues. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps (main effect thresholded at p < .05 FWE) and provides whole-brain exploratory results (coordinates/figures). Participant age and sex (male adolescents, ages 14–19), cue type (stimulants/cocaine/methamphetamine/drug paraphernalia), MRI field strength (1.5T mobile Siemens Avanto), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking versus matched control (teeth-brushing) stimuli (e.g., BEGIN: S2-T2, END: S4-T4) at the first level and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM5 with reported activations/deactivations (tables/figures described). Participant sex information and age-group comparisons are reported, scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (SPM5) are specified. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Based on this, the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (video clips). It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking vs. non-smoking videos (smoking>non-smoking), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using FSL (FLAME1) with thresholded Z-statistic maps and tables. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is nicotine, scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio) and processing software (FSL 5.0.9) are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images). It includes within-participant food>nonfood contrasts in a randomized, within-subject design and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected maps showing visual cortex differences). The paper provides participant age/sex details, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of visual drug-related cues (smoking) using a cue-exposure paradigm with within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM8) with FDR correction and results reported in text/tables/figures. Participant characteristics (male sample, ages reported in Table 1), cue type (nicotine/smoking), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8, FSL for DTI) are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward (food) cues with within-subject contrasts of food>non-food, reporting whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (tables/figures) analyzed with SPM2 on a 1.5T scanner. Participant sex is reported and participant ages are likely provided in Table 1 (subject characteristics) referenced in the full text; cue type (food), scanner field strength, and processing software are explicitly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual presentation (participants held a cigarette and viewed a live video feed). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of cigarette > control cues (main effect of cue) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables/figures and cluster-correction details. Relevant participant demographics (age range, sex distribution), cue type (cigarette/nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI, FSL, AIR, NIS) are reported. Full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual smoking images. The study reports within-subject contrasts comparing smoking-cue trials to control (no-distractor) and neutral trials, and conducts group-level, voxel-wise whole-brain analyses (random-effects repeated-measures ANOVA) with reported cluster thresholds. Results are presented as activation maps and tables with Talairach coordinates; figures and tables report whole-brain clusters. Participant age and sex distribution, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Thus it meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (meets I3) and includes within-participant food-vs-control contrasts (meets I4). However, the paper reports ROI and system-level ROI analyses (VS, OFC, and aggregated ROIs) and does not present or report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or tables of whole-brain peak coordinates in the provided full text. Therefore it meets Exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Additionally, the manuscript as provided does not explicitly report participant ages (only ‘undergraduate students’), so inclusion criterion I7 is not clearly satisfied. Full text appears complete. Exclusion reason: E3 (ROI-only results). Included: I3, I4. Not met: I5 (whole-brain voxelwise group map) and I7 (explicit age information).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood images, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (flexible factorial and two-sample t tests in SPM8) with tables/figures of activations. Methods report participant age and sex, cue type (food), 3.0T scanner field strength, and processing software (SPM8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of visual food cues with within-subject contrasts (food>control) and group-level whole-brain task results reported (exploratory whole-brain threshold, cluster coordinates/tables). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), and scanner field strength (3T) are reported. However, the full text does not explicitly report which fMRI processing/statistical software was used (e.g., SPM, FSL, AFNI) for image preprocessing and first-/second-level analyses; only stimulus presentation software (Presentation) and non-imaging stats software (HLM, SPSS) are named. Because inclusion criterion I7 (reporting processing software) is not satisfied, the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. If the authors’ MRI processing software were clearly reported or could be confirmed from supplementary material, the study would likely qualify for inclusion.

Full text is an observational/psychometric study without any fMRI cue-reactivity experiment or task activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported), I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise statistical maps), I6 (no whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures for task activation), I7 (while participant age/sex are reported, there is no information on cue type, MRI field strength, or processing software). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is ineligible for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (high-calorie food > brick walls). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM5 and reported with cluster/voxel results and figures. Relevant participant demographics (ages, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although sample size is small (n=3, leptin-deficient patients), this does not violate inclusion criteria. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (appetizing food images) with a within-subject contrast of appetizing > bland foods. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level SPM{t} maps are reported (thresholds and coordinates provided; Table 1 and figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence. The paper reports participant age range and sex breakdown, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). Although the study also includes PPI connectivity analyses, it additionally reports standard task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts, so it does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-subject task effects). Full-text methods, results, and discussion are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie foods vs objects and low-calorie vs objects). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain exploratory analyses are reported (cluster-corrected maps and peak coordinates in Table 4), meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL, FreeSurfer, ANTs, FEAT) are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete: provided content is a website privacy/cookie notice and article metadata only (title, authors, journal, DOI). Cannot verify that this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli, nor confirm within-participant cue>control contrasts, whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps, or reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, or processing software. Therefore cannot confirm inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7. Action: EXCLUDED due to incomplete/full-text not available for screening (fulltext_incomplete=true).

This is an fMRI empirical study of food (natural reward) cue-reactivity with within-participant contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results and adequate reporting (age/sex, cue type, scanner, software). However, it does not meet the review's stimulus modality requirement: cue presentation used personalized guided-imagery (auditory scripts) rather than visual stimuli. Therefore inclusion criterion I3 (use of visual stimuli) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cue-reactivity to visual natural rewards (erotic stimuli) in men seeking treatment for problematic pornography use. It reports within-participant cue-related contrasts (erotic vs control/non-reward cues), uses an ROI approach but also references whole-brain second-level contrasts (reported in Supplementary Figure S3), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (3T), and processing/toolbox information (MATLAB, MarsBaR, WFU PickAtlas). The full article contains Introduction, Methods (including fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion; supplementary whole-brain results are referenced (acceptable per I6). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for core content (supplementary figures/tables may be separate).

Although this is an fMRI study of visual food cue (natural reward) reactivity with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie food > nonfood) and reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM5), all core whole-brain task-evoked results appear to be reported using a predefined anatomical mask/regions-of-interest (insula and other food-related ROIs). The analyses and family-wise error corrections are described within that ROI mask; no unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or results are presented. Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and does not satisfy inclusion I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise map) or I6 (acceptable whole-brain reporting). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (LookSmoking > LookNeutral), and performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with corrected cluster thresholds; results are reported in tables and figures. Methods provide scanner field strength (Siemens Allegra 3.0T), processing software (SPM8; AlphaSim in AFNI), cue type (smoking/nicotine images), and participant characteristics (adults ≥18, Table 1). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food photographs) and reports within-subject contrasts (highly palatable > moderately palatable; high > neutral). Core article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present in the provided full text (supplemental materials are acceptable to be separate). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for core content.

This is an fMRI study of smokers using visual, smoking-related stimuli (graphic cigarette warning labels) with within-subject contrasts of LABEL>CONTROL and HIGH>LOW. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholded and cluster-corrected) with tables/figures of peak coordinates. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is nicotine-related (cigarette warnings), scanner field strength (3 T) and processing software (FSL) are specified. Although the stimuli are aversive/anti-smoking (graphic warnings) rather than appetitive drug cues, they are smoking-related visual cues and the study assesses craving change, so it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This study includes an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual methamphetamine-related images and reports within-subject contrasts (MA cues > neutral cues). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment against criteria.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos/images) and reports within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > non-smoking cues. However, all reported activation results were derived from region-of-interest (ROI) analyses using an ROI mask (mOFC, VS, amygdala, hippocampus, ACC, insula); there is no unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses) and does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain voxelwise group map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues (24 heroin-related vs 24 neutral images) with an event-related task and within-subject contrast heroin-related > neutral. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and post-hoc contrasts) are reported with correction (Monte Carlo) and regional results described in text/tables/figures. Relevant participant information (male participants, sample sizes per group, reference to age comparisons), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (DPARSF, SPM8, AFNI Monte Carlo) are reported. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not assess cue-reactivity to drug-related or natural reward-related cues in the sense required by the review. Specifically: (a) Exclusion IDs met: [] (no exclusion criteria triggered). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported with cluster correction and coordinates), I6 (whole-brain results are reported as coordinates/figures described in text), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type — nicotine-related context, scanner field strength = 3T, processing software = FSL — are reported). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (the study tests neural/behavioral responses to FDA graphic warning labels — aversive public-health images — not typical drug-related or natural reward-related cue stimuli intended to elicit reward-related cue-reactivity), and I4 (while there is a within-subject contrast graphic>non-graphic, this does not correspond to a drug-cue > control drug-cue contrast as required). Thus, although the paper uses visual stimuli and reports whole-brain fMRI contrasts in nicotine users, its stimuli are anti-smoking warning images (aversive health images) rather than drug-related reward cues; it does not meet the core conceptual inclusion criteria I3/I4 for a cue-reactivity meta-analysis.”}]}]}]}

This study is excluded because it does not assess cue-reactivity to drug-related or specified natural reward cues. (a) Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses and cluster results) and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures with coordinates). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/food/sexual cues — it uses monetary probabilistic cues), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug-cues>control or natural-reward-cues>control), and I7 (although age/sex, scanner field strength, and software are reported, the cue type is monetary and not among the cue categories required by the review). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the core eligibility for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (food and sexual images) with first-year female participants. It reports within-participant contrasts of reward cues versus baseline/control (food > baseline; sexual scenes > baseline) and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain regression results reported with coordinates and thresholding). Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength (3T Philips), and processing software (SPM2). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; whole-brain results are provided). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

The provided full text appears to be a narrative review or overview (title, abstract, keywords, and metadata) rather than an original empirical fMRI study. There is no methods, participants, experimental design, or results reporting original human fMRI data or cue-reactivity contrasts. Thus it does not provide whole-brain task activation maps or within-participant cue>control contrasts. Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata present). Excluded under E6 (non-empirical paper).

This study uses fMRI with visual food cues (natural reward) and reports within-subject contrasts (fattening > non-fattening), and provides participant demographics and scanner/processing details. However, it does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map; analyses focus on extracting mean ROI z-scores and ROI-based group comparisons. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward visual cues), I4 (within-participant contrast fattening>non-fattening), I7 (reported age/sex, cue type=food, scanner field strength=3T, and processing software=FSL). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map reported) and consequently I6 (no whole-brain results provided in tables/figures/coordinates). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Given these facts, the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study tested cue-reactivity using visual natural (erotic) and monetary stimuli in 38 participants, and reports within-subject contrasts (monetary cue > control; erotic cue > control). Results are reported as whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates; SPM2 preprocessing is specified and scanner field strength (1.5T), participant age and sex (heterosexual males; mean age reported) are provided. therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used gustatory (taste) alcohol cues (alcohol vs. juice) rather than visual stimuli, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I3 requiring visual cue stimuli. Relevant inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant alcohol>control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails I3 (visual-stimulus requirement).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (natural reward) with block-design cue exposure. The paper reports within-participant contrasts sex>neutral and sex>other rewards, performs group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with reported coordinates, figures, and statistical thresholds, and provides participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (3T Philips), and processing software (SPM5). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (smoking/nicotine) with both smokers and non-smokers. The authors report within-subject contrasts of smoking versus matched control stimuli (BEGIN- and END- smoking stimuli minus control stimuli) for task conditions (identification and distraction). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using FSL/FLAME with FWE-corrected thresholding; results are reported in tables, figures, and text. Relevant participant information (sex, group sizes, and age reported in group characteristics), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (FSL) are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task effects, empirical human fMRI data). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward (sexual) cues (I3). Within-participant contrasts of sexual cues versus neutral/emotional controls (S > NC/EC) are reported (I4). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level task-evoked maps reported via SPM12 with cluster results and MNI coordinates (I5,I6). Relevant participant and acquisition details are reported (male participants, age range inclusion 18–65, cue type sexual, 3-T scanner, SPM12 processing) fulfilling I7. No exclusion criteria are met: results include whole-brain task activation maps (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion reason (E3): The study reports results from ROI-restricted analyses (predefined ROIs using the WFU Pickatlas) and presents significant results only within these ROIs (Table 2); there is no clear unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of a natural reward — food — using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrasts of cue>control e.g., high-calorie vs fixation/neutral), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [SPM5] reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no evidence of reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task maps). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3. Full text completeness: full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images (I3). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food stimulus viewing versus baseline/fixation (e.g., Close + Far > baseline; stimulus-viewing regressors), satisfying the requirement for cue>control contrasts (I4). Group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM8; cluster thresholds with AlphaSim; tables/coordinates in supplement), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting via coordinates/figures (I5,I6). Relevant metadata are provided: participant ages and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) (I7). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental tables/coordinates are referenced. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to natural rewards using visual stimuli.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study using erotic (sexual) visual cues in humans, and reports group-level voxelwise results, so I3, I5 and I6 are satisfied. However, the study does not present a within-participant contrast of sexual cues > control (neutral) stimuli (no neutral/control visual cue condition is described), so I4 is not met. Also, the full text does not report MRI scanner field strength in the provided content, so I7 (reporting of scanner field strength) is not clearly met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because I4 and I7 are not satisfied.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and reports within-subject Food > Activities contrasts. The authors conducted and reported group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (thresholds and cluster FWE correction), with results presented in tables/figures and described in text. Participant age and sex distribution, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sugar-sweetened beverage) cue-reactivity that used visual stimuli (Coke product and logo advertisements). It includes within-subject contrasts of cue>control (Coke product ads > non-food ads; Coke logo ads > non-food ads), reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with appropriate multiple-comparison correction (cluster-wise pFWE, SPM8/AFNI procedures) and presents coordinates/tables and figures. Relevant participant details (adolescents, sample size, sex information), cue type (food/soft drink), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Allegra), and processing software (SPM8, AFNI modules) are reported. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) in children. The within-subject randomized crossover design modeled high- and low-calorie food blocks with blurred images as an implicit control baseline and conducted group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (ANOVA) with cluster correction using AFNI on a 3.0T scanner. The paper reports participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength, and processing software. Thus it meets criteria I3 (fMRI of natural reward visual cues), I4 (within-participant contrasts of cue conditions with blurred control implicitly modeled), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described), and I7 (reported age/sex, cue type, field strength, software). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (24 smoking-related pictures vs neutral pictures). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (craving vs neutral and regulation vs craving), and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is present, so fulltext appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (milkshake vs tasteless solution images). It includes within-participant contrasts of cue>control (unpaired milkshake cue – unpaired tasteless cue) and receipt contrasts (milkshake receipt – tasteless receipt). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (full-color food images). This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (fractal images) predicting food outcomes (natural reward). This full-text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (food images) with within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood control stimuli. This is an empirical fMRI study of visual food cue reactivity (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (food>neutral), group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and reported results in text/tables/figures. This manuscript is a study protocol describing planned fMRI analyses of visual food cues (natural reward) and meets I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrasts of Food vs control images are described). This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is included.

This study meets I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related cues using visual food stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrasts of fattening vs non-fattening/control stimuli), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type=food, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software). This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (chocolate pictures) and aversive cues, meeting the review focus. This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual sexual stimuli (erotic pictures) and conditioned visual cues. This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (infant faces) in mothers with substance addictions. This paper is a human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) in children (age/sex reported). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (BRAINVOYAGER) with cluster correction and peak coordinates/tables/figures. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, provides whole-brain task activations).

This is an empirical human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures). This study used an alcohol taste (gustatory) cue paradigm (Alcohol Taste > Water Taste); although brief visual labels preceded taste delivery, the primary cue modality was gustatory, not visual. The study is an imaging investigation of intranasal insulin effects using arterial spin labeling (resting CBF) and includes behavioral ratings of food pictures outside the scanner. It does not present a within-participant cue>control task contrast (no fMRI during visual food-cue presentation) nor a task-evoked whole-brain activation map for food cues. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant characteristics, cue type = food, scanner field strength, and processing software are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI assessment of cue-reactivity to visual stimuli during scanning), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded from the meta-analysis which requires task-evoked visual cue-reactivity contrasts/maps.

This full-text reports an fMRI study of a natural reward (chocolate) using visual stimuli (chocolate vs neutral pictures) with within-participant contrasts (chocolate > neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (random-effects ANOVAs, F-maps, cluster thresholds). Whole-brain results are reported with coordinates/tables and figures. Participant information includes sex (34 females) and age is described (undergraduate students; Table 1 reported group characteristics), cue type (food/chocolate), MRI scanner field strength (3 T Siemens Magnetom Allegra), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). The manuscript contains full Introduction/Methods/Results/Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3–I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual sexual cues (a natural reward) using pictures. It reports within-subject contrasts comparing sexual > neutral images (supraliminal and subliminal), and provides group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses using SPM5 with tables/figures/coordinates and standard voxelwise thresholds. Participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli as required. It uses a monetary incentive delay task probing reward anticipation for monetary rewards (symbolic cues), not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward images. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). (a) Exclusion criteria met: none. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables and text), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (fMRI assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues>control stimuli or natural reward-related cues>control stimuli). Therefore exclude.

This is an fMRI study but it does not assess cue-reactivity with visual stimuli. It measured resting cerebral blood flow (ASL) 4 h after consumption of high- vs low-GI meals (physiologic manipulation), not responses to visual drug or natural reward-related cues. Exclusion rationale: No within-participant contrasts of cue>control (I4 not met); no task-evoked cue-reactivity paradigm with visual stimuli (I3 not met); although voxelwise comparisons were performed, they are meal-condition comparisons rather than task-evoked whole-brain cue maps (I5/I6 not met). Reporting of participant age/sex and scanner/software is present, but cue type (visual cue) is absent, so I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Conclusion: study does not meet the required inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity visual-stimulus fMRI studies and is excluded.

This article is a narrative review summarizing PET and fMRI findings rather than reporting original human fMRI experiments. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper/review without original human fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an original fMRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli reported as original analyses), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map from an original fMRI dataset), I7 (does not report participant-level details for an original fMRI sample). Full text is complete (contains introduction, discussion, and review of prior studies). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study does not meet key inclusion requirements for the review. While it includes within-participant contrasts of reward cues vs neutral (anticipation of gain/loss vs neutral) and reports participant sex/age information, cue type (monetary), scanner field strength (1.5T) and processing software (SPM5) (I4 and I7 met), it fails to meet I3 and I5/I6: the cues are monetary (secondary/monetary incentive) rather than the drug or primary natural reward cue types specified in the review scope, and the study did not acquire or report a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map (analyses focused on a ventral striatal ROI; authors state whole-brain images were not acquired). Therefore E3 (ROI-only / no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I5, I6. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not address the review’s target cue types. The meta-analysis focuses on fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards (examples: nicotine, alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, heroin, food, sexual). This study uses monetary (secondary) reward anticipation (MID task) rather than drug or the natural reward cue types specified, so inclusion criterion I3 is not met. Likewise I7 is not met because the cue type is not among the listed reward categories required for eligibility, even though other details (age range, scanner field strength 1.5T, and processing software SPM8) are reported. The study does satisfy I4 (within-participant contrasts of reward cues > control), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity fMRI using visual stimuli and reports only ROI-based hypothalamic results rather than whole-brain task activation maps. Exclusion ID met: E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion IDs met: I7 (reported participant age/sex, cue type: food, scanner field strength: 3.0T, and processing software: FSL). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (the fMRI paradigm did not assess visual cue-reactivity; the fMRI measured hypothalamic response to oral glucose ingestion, while visual/odorous food exposure occurred outside/during fasting rather than as an fMRI task), I4 (no within-participant contrast of visual food cues > control stimuli was performed in the fMRI data), I5 (no group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map was reported; imaging was limited to a single midsagittal slice and analyses used a manually defined hypothalamic ROI), I6 (not applicable because no whole-brain results were presented). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of anticipatory monetary reward using visual cues (gain vs neutral) in smokers and non-smokers, and reports participant age/sex, cue type (monetary), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI) — meeting I3, I4, and I7. However, the reported neuroimaging results are presented as ROI/small-volume-corrected analyses within a priori reward ROIs; no unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain results are reported. Therefore it does not meet I5 and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

This study meets I3 (fMRI study of reward-related cue-reactivity using visual monetary cues in a MID task), I4 (within-participant contrasts of gain>neutral were performed), I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). However, I7 is not satisfied in the provided full text: participant sex is reported (9 males, 10 females) but participant age (mean or range) is not explicitly reported in the supplied content (Table 1 is referenced but its contents are not present here). Because I7 requires relevant information regarding participant age and sex, and age is not available in the provided document, the study does not meet all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The full text appears otherwise complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is false. Given the missing age information in the provided material, I exclude the study from the meta-analysis dataset.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (drug-related) with within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain results are reported with cluster-level thresholding and coordinates (Table 2) and figures. Methods report scanner field strength (Philips 3T) and processing software (BrainVoyager QX); participant demographics and age comparisons are referenced (Table 1), and cue type (alcohol) is explicit. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (visual drug cue fMRI, within-participant contrasts, whole-brain group maps, coordinate reporting, and relevant methodological details).

This is a resting-state fMRI pharmacological study of acute naltrexone effects on intrinsic functional connectivity, not a task-based cue-reactivity study. It does not present any drug- or natural-reward visual cue task, nor any within-participant cue>control contrast or whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (not a cue-reactivity visual-stimulus fMRI study), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I6 (not applicable—no task-based whole-brain results to report), I7 (while age/sex/scanner/software are reported, cue type and task details are not provided). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without whole-brain task activation). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion reason (E4): This study reports resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses and does not include any task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity contrast. Inclusion met: I7 (participant age/sex, cue type = food, MRI field strength = 3.0T, and processing software SPM8 are reported). Inclusion not met: I3 (no fMRI task assessing cue-reactivity with visual stimuli during scanning — images were presented after scanning), I4 (no within-participant task contrast of cues>control), I5 (no task-evoked, whole-brain group-level activation map). Therefore the paper must be excluded under E4.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (beer) cue-reactivity using visual cues (abstract shapes predicting beer vs water). It reports within-subject contrasts (beer>water) for anticipation (cue+delay), outcome notification, and delivery phases. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (T-maps, cluster-level FWE correction) and coordinates are provided; maps are available online. Key metadata are reported (participant age and sex, cue type: alcohol, 3T scanner, SPM8 processing). Full text includes Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete.

This article is a narrative review (non-empirical) summarizing neuroimaging studies and does not report original human fMRI task data. Exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical papers without original human fMRI data) applies. No inclusion criteria are met: I3 (an original fMRI study assessing cue-reactivity with visual stimuli) is not met; I4 (within-participant drug-cue>control contrast) is not met; I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) is not met; I6 (reporting of whole-brain results) is not met; I7 (reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner strength, processing software) is not met for an original dataset. Additionally, the provided full text is incomplete (abstract/introduction/references only), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a visual cue-reactivity task presenting alcohol, marijuana, polydrug, and appetitive (food, faces, landscapes) images and neutral controls. Within-subject contrasts comparing each cue type to neutral (e.g., alcohol>neutral, appetitive>neutral) are reported. Group-level, mixed-effects whole-brain analyses with cluster-based thresholding are described for the cue reactivity task, satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise reporting (thresholding and group maps described; results presented in text/figures). Required study details are provided: participant age and sex (mean age 18.92, 19 females), cue types, MRI scanner field strength (3.0T Siemens Magnetom Trio), and processing software (FSL v5.0). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol advertisements as cues with a within-subject ALCOHOL > CONTROL contrast. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses (ALCOHOL > CONTROL) with cluster-level multiple comparison correction and provides peak coordinates, tables, and figures. Participant demographics (age range and sex distribution), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8; AFNI’s 3dClustSim used for cluster correction) are all reported. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental materials are referenced but not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task study using visual e-cigarette advertising images (nicotine-related cues) and reports within-participant contrasts of e-cigarette > neutral images. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxelwise t-tests with cluster correction) were conducted and reported (tables/figures/supplement). Participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine/e-cigarette), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images). It reports within-subject contrasts (food vs. non-food; high-calorie vs. non-food) and group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM8 on 3.0T data. Results are reported with figures/tables and SVC/FWE-corrected voxelwise statistics within ROIs; whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses were performed and described. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength, and processing software are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3–I7) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual cues of natural reward (appetizing and disgusting food images) and reports within-participant contrasts (appetizing > bland/nonfood, disgusting > bland/nonfood) at the group (random-effects) level. Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were performed with results reported as statistical maps and peak coordinates; coordinates and thresholding are reported in text (and supplemental tables), and figures show activation overlays. Participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM99) are all reported. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies of natural rewards and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (pictures of candy/dessert) and within-subject contrasts. The task modeled food cue conditions relative to a low-level baseline (fixation) and conducted group-level, whole-brain second-level one-sample t-tests and factorial contrasts (e.g., LATER vs NOW, conditions vs baseline). Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported with coordinates and figures. Relevant participant details (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting, not non-empirical).

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using pictorial visual stimuli. It includes a within-subject contrast reflecting drug cues vs control (LCSP minus LCNP) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects RM-ANOVA and between-group t-tests) with reported coordinates and cluster results (Table 1 and figures). Results are reported using SPM8 on a 3T scanner; participant age and sex are provided. Although results use small-volume correction within a priori ROIs, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses were performed and coordinates/cluster statistics are reported, satisfying the meta-analysis reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts (food > nonfood; high-calorie > nonfood) fulfilling I3 and I4. However, the reported results are restricted to predefined ROIs using small-volume FWE correction; the paper does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or whole-brain results, so it fails I5 and thus meets exclusion E3 (only ROI-based results reported). Additionally, the full text as provided does not clearly report participant sex (I7 not verifiable from text). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED due to E3 (and missing I5/I7).

Provided "full text" is incomplete (a redirect/metadata page only). Core article content (methods, results) is not present, so I cannot verify key inclusion criteria. Cannot confirm that this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (I3), that it reports within-participant contrasts of cues>control (I4), that it includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps (I5/I6), or that participant/cue/scanner/software details are reported (I7). Therefore the study cannot be assessed for inclusion and is excluded due to incomplete full text preventing verification of all inclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used visual cues (participant-supplied photographs of the rejecting beloved vs a familiar neutral face) and reports a within-subject contrast (rejecter > neutral). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and whole-brain exploratory results are reported (thresholded at P<0.001 uncorrected) with coordinates/tables described in the text and tables. Participant age and sex are reported (mean age 19.8, 10 women/5 men), cue type (romantic/partner images, a natural reward-related cue), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM2) are all provided. Although ROI analyses are emphasized, whole-brain task-evoked results are also reported, so the study is not excluded for ROI-only reporting. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual/abstract cues (basket images), with within-subject contrasts comparing high vs no food reward (10 SP vs 0 SP). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected results and supplementary tables/figures) and ROI plus whole-brain results. Participant demographics (age ranges, sex matching), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T Tim Trio), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli in humans. It reports within-subject contrasts of food-related stimuli (high/low caloric food blocks) relative to baseline and examines changes across conditions (glucose vs. water) and timepoints. Group-level whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses were conducted using SPM8 and whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures (clusters, coordinates, and thresholding). Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). Hence the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol that meets several inclusion criteria (within-participant alcohol>control contrast; group-level, voxelwise analysis with reported peak coordinates; reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). However, it does NOT meet I3 because the cue modality is gustatory (alcohol taste vs litchi juice) rather than visual stimuli, and the meta-analysis specifically requires visual cue paradigms. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to visual-stimulus cue-reactivity studies.
